books.title: What My MBA Did Not Teach Me About Money
books.subtitle: The Human and Financial Perspective of Money, Finance, Markets, People, and Life
books.authorRole: Founder, Modulor Capital & Founder, Sahayak Associates
books.description: A practical exploration of the human and financial side of money, helping readers understand money beliefs, investing, financial biases, risk, budgeting and better financial decision-making.
aboutBook: How we think about money can be very different from how we feel about it. While financial concepts may appear simple on paper, budgeting, financial conversations, risk calculation, investment discipline and wealth preservation can often be challenging.
What My MBA Did Not Teach Me About Money presents practical strategies around money beliefs, financial challenges, stock market investing, personal biases and financial vulnerability.

The ideas are based on the authors’ practical experiences and their work advising clients, with the aim of bridging the gap between the emotional human perspective and the analytical financial perspective of money.
whatYouWillLearn: Bridge emotional and logical approaches to money

samplePages.title: The Emotion Behind the Balance Sheet
content: Money is rarely just about numbers. It is an emotional landscape shaped by upbringing, societal expectations, and core internal drivers.
Before we can master compound interest or asset allocation, we must first understand the narratives we tell ourselves about wealth, risk, and security.

books.description:
Turning 18 is the beginning of a new chapter — a step into adulthood filled with greater freedom, new responsibilities, important choices and life-changing experiences.

“Heyy 18: What an 18 Year Old Should Know” brings together 52 practical life lessons designed to guide young adults through one of the most important stages of life.

Thoughtful, relatable and easy to read, the book encourages young readers to reflect on their values, understand their choices and approach adulthood with greater confidence, wisdom and purpose.

blogs.title: The Future of Constitutional Jurisprudence in the AI Era
blogs.excerpt: How algorithms and predictive decision systems are challenging foundational principles of natural justice and administrative transparency.
content: As machine intelligence penetrates judicial drafting, credit scoring, and municipal resource allocation, the bedrock legal doctrine of Audi Alteram Partem (listen to the other side) faces an unprecedented test.

When an opaque neural network generates a determination affecting citizen liberty or corporate licensing, who bears the burden of explainability? Our latest research at Sahayak Associates establishes three critical legal standards for algorithmic accountability.

First, no administrative order may be enforced without human supervisory sign-off. Second, the training data provenance must be accessible during judicial review. Third, algorithmic bias audits must be made mandatory across public governance portfolios.

blogs.seoTitle: Constitutional Jurisprudence in the AI Era | Sahayak Books
blogs.metaDescription: Explore the intersection of machine learning and constitutional rights by Adv. Meenakshi Sundaram.

blogs.title: Deconstructing Monetary Policy Transmission in Emerging Markets
blogs.excerpt: An empirical analysis of how repo rate adjustments influence commercial lending rates and capital investment velocity.
content: The conventional textbook view assumes an instant pass-through from central bank policy rates to commercial banking loan books. In reality, structural liquidity friction, statutory liquidity ratios, and asset-liability mismatches create substantial transmission lag.

In this detailed commentary, Dr. Rajeshwar Sen examines why traditional fiscal levers behave differently in emerging economic corridors and how corporate treasuries can hedge interest rate volatility proactively.
blogs.author: Dr. Rajeshwar Sen
blogs.seoTitle: Monetary Policy Transmission in Emerging Markets | Sahayak Insights
blogs.metaDescription: Dr. Rajeshwar Sen on central banking transmission and macro volatility.

blogs.title: Mastering the Art of High-Stakes Negotiation & Calm Authority
blogs.excerpt: Why the most powerful negotiator in the room is often the one who speaks least, listens deeply, and controls internal arousal levels.
content: Negotiation is fundamentally an exercise in emotional regulation. When billions of rupees or key policy covenants hang in the balance, amateur negotiators rely on aggressive rhetoric or artificial urgency.

Master negotiators, by contrast, practice the art of strategic silence, precision paraphrasing, and asymmetrical value concession. Learn the 4-phase preparation framework taught at Sahayak Associates Executive Retreats.
blogs.author: Priya Malhotra
blogs.metaDescription: Executive coach Priya Malhotra on calmness, authority, and negotiation mastery.
